rootCause.class: run construction (driver / composition), not product behaviour
rootCause.what: The driver's main.yaml declares the leader with `capabilities.builtinToolDeny: []`, while the World always composes the `u5-canary` and `u6-fs-probe-host` test rows (composed profile: log lines 1-5). Those two rows put `u5_canary` and `u6fs_probe` on the leader's final model-facing surface.
rootCause.why: The product's A2C-2 permission coverage gate refuses to start the root agent when any model-facing tool is neither allowed, asked, nor denied — `unknown-unmanaged` is exactly that state. So `team.create` was refused before a leader session existed, and no member, no delegate, no tool call, and no PTY ever ran.
rootCause.where: dev/agent-workflow/evidence/a5sf-bl17-live2/run-boot.mjs, mainBlueprintYaml(), the line `'    builtinToolDeny: []'` (line 152 of the copied driver).
canonicalPatternNotFollowed: tests/world-factory/lib/u6-fs-assembly.mjs:154-162 — `mainBlueprintYaml(denyList)` puts EVERY unmanaged name on the final model-facing surface into `builtinToolDeny`, with the measured b2 comment: deny is coverage here, not a call site.

tests/world-factory/suites/040-u6-arc-a.mjs:159-161 — discovery prompt first, read `surfaceNamesOf(mock request)`, compute `denyList = surface.filter(not team_ && not MANAGED && not SAFE_UNMANAGED)`, write main.yaml, then `team.create`.
rootCause.notProduct: The gate produced the documented diagnostic with the documented inner code and named both tools. Nothing here contradicts any host-free arm: the arms never claim a coverage-clean leader surface, and the a5sf-bash README §8 checklist (which starts at the native module mount) does not mention the world's canary/probe rows at all.

This run's fixed driver passed that point (the pre-create state read is diagnostic-only and really did continue: see `preCreateState` below), then died at the first step the boot-3 run never reached. Each fix moves the failure to the next unexercised construction step.

preflightCouldNotSee.verdictItGave: PASS 16/16 (including driver.gate-order PASS, driver.log-capture PASS, bundle.case-coverage PASS) — a genuine PASS on everything it declares, and still insufficient.
preflightCouldNotSee.blindSpot: The bundle declares blueprint IDs and member counts (`identity.blueprints`) but never the leader's model-facing tool surface nor its permission coverage. The driver's blueprint text lives inside the driver; it is not a bundle fact. No check compares `builtinToolDeny` against the World's always-composed test rows (`u5-canary`, `u6-fs-probe-host`), and the driver never discovers the surface before create.
whatWouldHaveCaughtIt: A `driver.leader-surface` check over a declared `driver.blueprint.leaderSurface = { tools: [...], builtinToolDeny: [...], managed: [...] }` requiring every non-team tool in the declared surface to be covered. The world rows are known before boot (the factory composes them), so this is a host-free-checkable declaration.

Or a declared step `discover-leader-surface` whose `produces: ['leader-surface']` must precede `create-team`, with the create step's `requires: ['leader-surface']` — the same declared-precondition mechanism as driver.gate-order, extended to the surface fact.
Neither exists today. This is the same structural lesson as boot #3: a content-complete bundle can still omit the fact that the next gate consumes.
